_comment: Original practice dialogues written for this app, built around the chapter 1-3 glossary words (not copied from the textbook). Markup in 'fi': [word] marks a glossary word written exactly as in the glossary; [surface](lemma) marks an inflected form, where lemma is the glossary entry. Tapping a marked word shows its meaning and pronunciation.

conversations.title: Uusi kurssi
conversations.subtitle: A new course: greetings, names and spelling

lines.en: Hi! Excuse me, is this seat free?
Yes, it is.
Nice. I'm Sofia.
I'm Leo. Nice to meet you!
Likewise! Is the Finnish course here?
Yes. This is Finnish 1.
Hi, Leo! How are you?
Hey, Matti! Just fine, thanks. And you?
I'm fine.
Hi and welcome! My name is Liisa Virtanen. I'm your teacher.
Excuse me, how is it spelled?
The first name is L-I-I-S-A and the last name V-I-R-T-A-N-E-N.
The course is at 18–20. It ends at 20.
Thank you!

conversations.title: Jäätelökioskilla
conversations.subtitle: At the ice-cream kiosk: prices, spoken numbers, card or cash

lines.en: Hi!
Hi. How much is one scoop?

lines.fi: Yks [pallo] [maksaa] kolme euroo, kaks [palloo](pallo) viis euroo.
lines.en: One scoop costs three euros, two scoops five euros.
OK. I'll take one scoop of strawberry.
I'll take two scoops: chocolate and strawberry.
Sure. Anything else?
No, thanks.
Eight euros in total. Cash or card?
By card, please. I'll pay for these.
Do you need a receipt?
No, thanks.
Thanks, Sofia! Next time I'll pay.

conversations.title: Mistä sinä olet kotoisin?
conversations.subtitle: In the park: countries, languages and getting home

lines.en: Sofia, where are you from?
I'm from Italy. How about you?
I'm Finnish, but my mother is Swedish.
I'm from Canada. My mother tongue is English.
Do you also speak French?
A little. I don't speak French well.
My mother tongue is Italian. What languages do you speak, Matti?
Finnish, Swedish and English.
Where do you live, Leo?
I live in Helsinki. I go home by bus.

lines.fi: [Minä] en asu Helsingissä [vaan](ei X vaan Y) Espoossa. [Minä] [ajan](ajaa) [autolla](auto).
lines.en: I don't live in Helsinki but in Espoo. I drive.
Oh yeah, true! See you tomorrow!

conversations.title: Videopuhelu
conversations.subtitle: Practice for the book text “Pedro soittaa Mikolle” (s. 57): work, weather, the course and moving

lines.fi: [Moi](Hei! / Moi!), Ville! Mitä sinne kuuluu? Oletko [jo] [töissä](olla töissä)?
lines.en: Hi, Ville! How are things there? Are you at work already?

lines.fi: [Moi](Hei! / Moi!)! [Ei vielä]. Täällä [kello] on [vasta] [puoli] seitsemän. Juon aamukahvia.
lines.en: Hi! Not yet. Here it's only half past six. I'm drinking my morning coffee.
Oh right! It's still morning in Canada.
The weather here is quite bad. It's raining and windy. And in Finland?
Here the sun is shining and it's really warm, twenty-two degrees.
In summer the night is so bright that it's hard for me to sleep.
Enjoy it now! In November it's really dark again.
So I hear.
What else? Do you have a job already?

lines.fi: [Ei vielä]. [Etsin töitä](etsiä töitä) joka päivä, [mutta] se ei ole [helppoa](helppo). [Nyt] olen suomen kurssilla.
lines.en: Not yet. I look for work every day, but it isn't easy. Now I'm on a Finnish course.
That's great! What's the course like?

lines.fi: [Tosi] [mukava]. Opettaja on hauska, [ja] minun naapurini on [samalla](sama) kurssilla. Tunnit ovat [maanantaisin], [keskiviikkoisin] [ja] [torstaisin].
lines.en: Really nice. The teacher is fun, and my neighbour is on the same course. Lessons are on Mondays, Wednesdays and Thursdays.

lines.fi: Kolme [kertaa](kerta) viikossa! Pian sinä puhut suomea [yhtä hyvin kuin] minä.
lines.en: Three times a week! Soon you'll speak Finnish as well as I do.
Ha ha, maybe some day.
Do you still live in the student apartment in Tampere?
Yes, but we're moving in September. Our new home is in Vantaa.

lines.fi: [Kuulostaa hyvältä]! Hei, [nyt] [minun täytyy] [lähteä töihin]. [Terveisiä Liisalle!](Terveisiä Hannalle!)
lines.en: Sounds good! Hey, now I have to leave for work. Say hi to Liisa!
Thanks, I'll tell her! Bye bye!
Bye bye!

conversations.title: Kurssitoimistossa
conversations.subtitle: Practice for the book dialogue “Pedro ilmoittautuu kurssille” (kpl 3): signing up for a course

lines.en: Hi! How can I help?
Hi! I'd like to enrol on a Finnish course, level one.
OK. The next Finnish 1 course already starts next Monday.

lines.fi: [Ensi] maanantaina? Voi ei, silloin olen matkalla. [Se ei käy].
lines.en: Next Monday? Oh no, I'm travelling then. That doesn't work.
Well, another course starts in October.

lines.fi: Lokakuu sopii hyvin. Onko kurssilla [vielä] tilaa?
lines.en: October suits me well. Is there still room on the course?
Just a moment, I'll check… Yes, there are still a couple of free places.
Good, thanks!
What's your name?
Leo Martins.
Sorry, can you say that again?

lines.fi: [Etunimi] on Leo, [sukunimi] on Martins. M – A – R – T – I – N – S.
lines.en: My first name is Leo, my last name is Martins. M – A – R – T – I – N – S.

lines.fi: Kiitos. [Tässä] on [lomake]. Kirjoita tähän sinun tietosi.
lines.en: Thanks. Here's a form. Write your details here.
OK, thanks.
Excuse me, can you help? What does “postinumero” mean?

lines.fi: Se on viisi numeroa ennen [kaupungin](kaupunki) nimeä, esimerkiksi 00100 Helsinki.
lines.en: It's the five numbers before the city name, for example 00100 Helsinki.

lines.fi: Aa, minulla se on 02150 Espoo. Nyt lomake on [valmis]. [Kiitos avusta]!
lines.en: Ah, mine is 02150 Espoo. Now the form is ready. Thanks for the help!
You're welcome. The registration is done. You'll get the invoice by e-mail next week.
OK, thanks. Bye!
